Web + iOS · Wisconsin Creative · 2026-09-25

Your Day on Home

Home now answers what needs you right now, what's next, and what your week looks like. Shifts and their gear sit together in one place.

iOS Home, worked events

Same homeAgenda fixture, device, appearance and scroll. The before image was built from an isolated HEAD worktree with only the fixture and test files copied in. Timestamps differ by minutes because the fixture is relative to the capture hour.

Top of Home

Staff user with a game tonight, a road game tomorrow with gear reserved, and a return Sunday.

Web dashboard, Your day

After-only: none of this existed before. Same static render and fixture.

What changed, and why

Shifts and gear lived apart

Was

Web listed a reservation both under My reservations and as a badge on its shift. iOS hid event-linked gear from Home entirely.

Now

Each worked event carries its own gear state on both platforms, and My reservations drops what an event card already shows.

Nothing said what needs you now

Was

Urgency was spread across stat tiles, lane colours, and the queue.

Now

At most one banner, in a fixed order: your overdue gear, your pickup, today's game with no gear, a return due later today. Dismissal lasts the day. Web and iOS share the order and wording (parity test).

No sense of the week

Was

Web had no time-aware section; iOS showed only Next Up rows.

Now

A seven-day strip on both platforms and a Next up card with a countdown on web. Staff events anchor on the event start and never name a call time.

Nudges were invisible to colleagues

Was

A nudge's sent state lived in one screen's memory.

Now

Overdue rows and Booking detail show "Nudged 20m ago by …" from the audit log, and within the hour the button reads as sent.

Verification

  • Full vitest suite: 701 files, 4,969 tests pass, including new home-agenda (14), home-agenda-parity (4), and nudge-history (6) tests, plus four updated Home contracts.
  • TypeScript, ESLint, npm run build:app, verify:docs, and git diff --check all pass.
  • Wisconsin iOS simulator build passes. HomeScreenshotUITests capture on the dedicated iPhone 18 Pro Max capture device; ios:project:check passes after regenerating with XcodeGen and restoring the schemes.

Things to know

  • No signed-in web check: this branch has no preview environment until its PR runs Managed previews.
  • iOS captures use fixtures, so they only show presentation. The personal pickups field (myPendingPickups) and the 10-shift payload need a real signed-in check.
  • iOS keeps its existing Next Up queue rather than adding a separate Next up card.
